practice_name: Maize + greengram alternate-row intercropping
description: Greengram grown in alternate rows with maize at 75 x 20 cm spacing under rainfed conditions; gave the best overall productivity index and good net returns
source: Sridhar H S & Salakinkop S R, Competitive functions, pest dynamics and bio-economic analysis in traditional maize and legumes intercropping systems under rainfed situation of South India, Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge 20(3), 2021, pp 827-837

practice_name: Maize + blackgram alternate-row intercropping
description: Blackgram (urdbean) grown in alternate rows with maize at 75 x 20 cm spacing; gave the highest maize-equivalent yield and net returns of all systems tested
source: Sridhar H S & Salakinkop S R, Competitive functions, pest dynamics and bio-economic analysis in traditional maize and legumes intercropping systems under rainfed situation of South India, Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge 20(3), 2021, pp 827-837

practice_name: Maize + cowpea intercropping
description: Cowpea grown between maize rows; its early canopy smothers weeds but it competes strongly with maize, so returns were lower than with blackgram or greengram
source: Sridhar H S & Salakinkop S R, Competitive functions, pest dynamics and bio-economic analysis in traditional maize and legumes intercropping systems under rainfed situation of South India, Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge 20(3), 2021, pp 827-837

practice_name: Legume intercropping to reduce fall armyworm in maize
description: Growing legumes between maize rows lowered fall armyworm attack compared with sole maize; crop diversity confuses the moths and legumes help repel them
source: Sridhar H S & Salakinkop S R, Competitive functions, pest dynamics and bio-economic analysis in traditional maize and legumes intercropping systems under rainfed situation of South India, Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge 20(3), 2021, pp 827-837

practice_name: Arecanut-based intercropping with coconut, nutmeg and banana (with dairy cows)
region: Kumta and Honnavar, Uttara Kannada, Karnataka
description: Coconut on the borders and nutmeg and banana between the arecanut palms, combined with cows whose dung is recycled as farm manure; gave higher returns than arecanut alone
source: Bhat S, Kumar D, Paramesh V, et al., Enhancing farm profitability and sustainability through integrated farming systems: A case study of coastal Karnataka, India, Farming System 1 (2023) 100052, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.farsys.2023.100052

practice_name: Neem leaf extract spray
description: Fresh neem leaves are soaked overnight, ground, filtered and diluted in water before spraying; farmers use it against leaf-eating and sucking pests
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Garlic extract spray
description: Ground garlic is soaked overnight, squeezed through muslin and made up with water; used against leaf-eating caterpillars and fruit borers
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Garlic-chilli extract spray
description: Equal amounts of garlic and green chilli are ground and soaked separately overnight then mixed into a 3 per cent solution; used against fruit borers and brinjal shoot and fruit borer
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Fermented cow dung-urine-leaf botanical spray
description: Cow dung and urine are fermented with calotropis, vitex, neem, adhatoda and pongamia leaves in a barrel for four weeks then filtered and diluted; a variant of the old kunapajala preparation used against borers and tobacco caterpillar
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Adhatoda leaf extract spray
description: Adhatoda leaves are ground in water and left for a day before filtering and spraying against defoliators and sucking pests
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Datura plant extract spray
description: Dried datura leaves and pods are powdered and soaked in water for a day then filtered; used against tea mosquito bug thrips jassids and aphids
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Ekka (calotropis) leaf extract for termites
description: Sun-dried ekka leaves are powdered and soaked in water for a day then filtered and applied to manage termites
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Lantana powder and leaf extract spray
description: Dried lantana branches with leaves and young fruits are powdered for use against aphids while a fresh leaf extract is used against beetles leaf miners and defoliators
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Mixed leaves in cow urine extract
description: Leaves of custard apple papaya pomegranate guava neem and pongamia are crushed in cow urine boiled down to half then filtered and diluted; used against defoliators such as tobacco caterpillar and semi-loopers
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Panchapatre leaf and cow urine spray
description: Leaves of calotropis neem adhatoda and vitex are ground with cow urine and asafetida in a closed drum and used after a week; applied against defoliators fruit borers aphids and whiteflies
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Nilgiri (eucalyptus) leaf extract spray
description: Tender eucalyptus leaves are boiled for about an hour then filtered and diluted before spraying against jassids aphids and scales
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Chilli-neem-garlic extract for pigeonpea pests
description: Chilli neem leaves and garlic paste in a 1:4:1 ratio are boiled in water filtered and diluted; farmers use it against caterpillar pests of pigeonpea
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Multiple plant fermented extract applied through irrigation water
description: Cow dung and urine with calotropis parthenium lantana datura pongamia cake neem kernel extract jaggery and ash are fermented for a week then filtered and applied through irrigation water against major pests and diseases
source: Raghavendra K V, Gowthami R, Lepakshi N M, Dhananivetha M & Shashank R, Use of Botanicals by Farmers for Integrated Pest Management of Crops in Karnataka, Asian Agri-History 20(3), 2016, pp 173-180

practice_name: Legume rotation in organic chilli and tomato
region: Athani, Chikkodi, Gokak and Hukkeri taluks, Belgaum, Karnataka
description: All surveyed organic growers rotated chilli and tomato with a legume crop such as soybean or cowpea as part of managing pests and diseases
source: Patil M, Bheemappa A, Angadi J G & Arvindkumar B N, Production and post harvest management practices followed in organic vegetable cultivation, Karnataka Journal of Agricultural Sciences 23(2), 2010, pp 269-273

practice_name: Marigold trap cropping in chilli and tomato
region: Athani, Chikkodi, Gokak and Hukkeri taluks, Belgaum, Karnataka
description: Marigold is grown as a trap crop in organic chilli and tomato fields to draw pests away from the main crop; about 86 per cent of growers used it
source: Patil M, Bheemappa A, Angadi J G & Arvindkumar B N, Production and post harvest management practices followed in organic vegetable cultivation, Karnataka Journal of Agricultural Sciences 23(2), 2010, pp 269-273

practice_name: Neem seed kernel extract and neem cake in organic vegetables
region: Athani, Chikkodi, Gokak and Hukkeri taluks, Belgaum, Karnataka
description: Neem seed kernel extract is sprayed against worms and whiteflies (about 91 per cent of growers) and neem cake is applied at transplanting against nematodes and root diseases (about 41 per cent)
source: Patil M, Bheemappa A, Angadi J G & Arvindkumar B N, Production and post harvest management practices followed in organic vegetable cultivation, Karnataka Journal of Agricultural Sciences 23(2), 2010, pp 269-273

practice_name: Conserving predators with bird perches
region: Athani, Chikkodi, Gokak and Hukkeri taluks, Belgaum, Karnataka
description: Growers protect natural predators in the field (97 per cent) and a few put up bird perches of jowar stalks or tree branches so crows and mynas feed on pests
source: Patil M, Bheemappa A, Angadi J G & Arvindkumar B N, Production and post harvest management practices followed in organic vegetable cultivation, Karnataka Journal of Agricultural Sciences 23(2), 2010, pp 269-273

practice_name: Panchagavya and beejamrut seed treatment
region: Athani, Chikkodi, Gokak and Hukkeri taluks, Belgaum, Karnataka
description: Seeds are treated with panchagavya or beejamrut an old practice believed to build resistance to pests and disease and support growth; used by about 59 per cent of growers
source: Patil M, Bheemappa A, Angadi J G & Arvindkumar B N, Production and post harvest management practices followed in organic vegetable cultivation, Karnataka Journal of Agricultural Sciences 23(2), 2010, pp 269-273

practice_name: Ash and cow dung slurry applied with irrigation
region: Athani, Chikkodi, Gokak and Hukkeri taluks, Belgaum, Karnataka
description: Ash and cow dung slurry are applied along with irrigation water as a home-made biodigester input for pest and disease management; about 27 per cent of growers used it
source: Patil M, Bheemappa A, Angadi J G & Arvindkumar B N, Production and post harvest management practices followed in organic vegetable cultivation, Karnataka Journal of Agricultural Sciences 23(2), 2010, pp 269-273

practice_name: Mixed cropping of chilli and tomato with companion crops
region: Athani, Chikkodi, Gokak and Hukkeri taluks, Belgaum, Karnataka
description: Chilli and tomato are grown mixed with companions such as coriander onion garlic maize or castor which most growers used to reduce pests and the risk of crop failure
source: Patil M, Bheemappa A, Angadi J G & Arvindkumar B N, Production and post harvest management practices followed in organic vegetable cultivation, Karnataka Journal of Agricultural Sciences 23(2), 2010, pp 269-273

practice_name: River anicuts of unmortared stone
region: Bellary and Raichur districts (Tungabhadra river), Karnataka
description: Low stone weirs of 4 to 8 feet built across the river using rocky islands and laid without lime mortar so silt could pass through the joints; they raise the water level to feed canals
source: Shivakumar M G & Cheluvaraju R, Ancient Irrigation Systems of Karnataka (journal and year not shown in the PDF text; add from the paper)

practice_name: Series (cascade) tanks with sluice and waste weir
region: Bellary and Raichur districts (Vijayanagara region), Karnataka
description: Tanks were built one after another on the same stream so surplus water from one fed the next lower tank; each had a stone-faced embankment sluices and a waste weir
source: Shivakumar M G & Cheluvaraju R, Ancient Irrigation Systems of Karnataka (journal and year not shown in the PDF text; add from the paper)

practice_name: Open and spring wells with stone aqueduct conveyance
region: Bellary and Raichur districts (Vijayanagara region), Karnataka
description: Individuals dug open and spring wells in areas not served by anicuts or tanks and carried the water in canals on stone aqueducts and burnt clay pipes
source: Shivakumar M G & Cheluvaraju R, Ancient Irrigation Systems of Karnataka (journal and year not shown in the PDF text; add from the paper)

practice_name: Bullock and labour water lifts
region: Bellary and Raichur districts (Vijayanagara region), Karnataka
description: Where fields lay above the water in wells rivers or streams farmers lifted water using labour or bullocks and sometimes water wheels to irrigate small areas
source: Shivakumar M G & Cheluvaraju R, Ancient Irrigation Systems of Karnataka (journal and year not shown in the PDF text; add from the paper)

practice_name: Tank-irrigated kharif and rabi cropping in Bagalkot
description: Farmers in tank commands grow kharif and rabi crops with sorghum as the main food crop and reach a cropping intensity of about 198 per cent
source: Suresh E, Economic analysis of cropping systems under tank irrigation in Northern Karnataka, M.Sc. (Agri.) thesis, University of Agricultural Sciences Dharwad, 2010

practice_name: Tank-irrigated kharif rabi and summer cropping in Bijapur
description: Tank command farmers grow crops in kharif rabi and also summer seasons; tank committees exist but farmers report inadequate water and poor tank maintenance
source: Suresh E, Economic analysis of cropping systems under tank irrigation in Northern Karnataka, M.Sc. (Agri.) thesis, University of Agricultural Sciences Dharwad, 2010

practice_name: Maize + redgram cropping system
description: Maize and redgram grown together under rainfed conditions; it gave net returns of about Rs 22513 per ha and a benefit-cost ratio of 1.84
source: Kumara B R, Economics of cropping systems under rainfed situations in Belgaum and Dharwad districts of Karnataka, M.Sc. (Agri.) thesis, University of Agricultural Sciences Dharwad, 2011

practice_name: Sorghum + redgram cropping system
description: Sorghum and redgram grown together under rainfed conditions; it was the most profitable system with net returns of about Rs 24659 per ha and a benefit-cost ratio of 2.01
source: Kumara B R, Economics of cropping systems under rainfed situations in Belgaum and Dharwad districts of Karnataka, M.Sc. (Agri.) thesis, University of Agricultural Sciences Dharwad, 2011

practice_name: Greengram + redgram cropping system
description: Greengram and redgram grown together under rainfed conditions; it gave the lowest returns of the three combinations at about Rs 12507 per ha with a benefit-cost ratio of 1.47
source: Kumara B R, Economics of cropping systems under rainfed situations in Belgaum and Dharwad districts of Karnataka, M.Sc. (Agri.) thesis, University of Agricultural Sciences Dharwad, 2011

practice_name: Akkadi mixed cropping with finger millet or groundnut
region: Chikkamaranahalli cluster villages, Nelamangala taluk, Bengaluru Rural, Karnataka
description: Farmers grow 10 to 14 rows of finger millet or groundnut followed by one row of a mix of 5 to 9 other crops in no fixed proportion; the paper notes the mixed crops compete and mature at different times
source: Ramachandrappa B K, Thimmegowda M N, Sathish A, Jagadeesh B N, Devaraja K, Srikanth Babu P N & Savitha M S, Real Time Contingency Measures to Cope with Rainfall Variability in Southern Karnataka, Indian Journal of Dryland Agricultural Research and Development 31(1), 2016, pp 37-43

practice_name: Finger millet + pigeonpea (8:2) with conservation furrow
region: Chikkamaranahalli cluster villages, Nelamangala taluk, Bengaluru Rural, Karnataka
description: An improved form of the farmers' mixed cropping where pigeonpea is sown in paired rows with a furrow between them to hold rain; it gave a mean finger millet equivalent yield of 2749 kg per ha against 1774 kg under farmers' practice
source: Ramachandrappa B K, Thimmegowda M N, Sathish A, Jagadeesh B N, Devaraja K, Srikanth Babu P N & Savitha M S, Real Time Contingency Measures to Cope with Rainfall Variability in Southern Karnataka, Indian Journal of Dryland Agricultural Research and Development 31(1), 2016, pp 37-43

practice_name: Groundnut + pigeonpea (8:2) with conservation furrow
region: Chikkamaranahalli cluster villages, Nelamangala taluk, Bengaluru Rural, Karnataka
description: Groundnut and pigeonpea sown in 8:2 rows with a moisture-conserving furrow between pigeonpea rows; it gave a mean groundnut equivalent yield of 1347 kg per ha against 473 kg for sole groundnut
source: Ramachandrappa B K, Thimmegowda M N, Sathish A, Jagadeesh B N, Devaraja K, Srikanth Babu P N & Savitha M S, Real Time Contingency Measures to Cope with Rainfall Variability in Southern Karnataka, Indian Journal of Dryland Agricultural Research and Development 31(1), 2016, pp 37-43

practice_name: Groundnut-finger millet rotation with farmyard manure
description: Groundnut and finger millet were grown in alternate years for 13 years with 10 t per ha of farmyard manure; manure alone matched full chemical fertiliser and yields kept rising over time
source: Srinivasarao Ch, Ramachandrappa B K, Jakkula V S, Kundu S, Venkateswarlu B, Pharande A L, Manideep V R, Naik R P & Venkanna K, Nutrient Balance after Thirteen Years of Organic and Chemical Nutrient Management and Yield Sustainability of Groundnut-Fingermillet Rotation in Rainfed Alfisols of Semi-Arid India, Journal of the Indian Society of Soil Science 62(3), 2014, pp 235-247

practice_name: Kharif crop followed by rabi legume with block rotation
description: Finger millet was followed by field bean and maize with cowpea was followed by horsegram in rabi, and crops were rotated between blocks to keep soil-borne pests and diseases down and protect soil health
source: Mahadevaswamy M, Shenoi M M, Ramesh S, Mahadeva C & Venkatesh T, Sustainable livelihood through agro-forestry and livestock based integrated farming system in rainfed Alfisols of Southern Transitional Zone of Karnataka, Agriculture for Sustainable Development 2(2), 2014, pp 97-100

practice_name: Maize + cowpea (1:1) intercropping
description: Hybrid maize and cowpea grown in a 1:1 arrangement in kharif then horsegram in rabi; this block gave lower returns than the cotton and redgram plus groundnut block
source: Mahadevaswamy M, Shenoi M M, Ramesh S, Mahadeva C & Venkatesh T, Sustainable livelihood through agro-forestry and livestock based integrated farming system in rainfed Alfisols of Southern Transitional Zone of Karnataka, Agriculture for Sustainable Development 2(2), 2014, pp 97-100

practice_name: Redgram + groundnut (2:8) intercropping
description: Redgram and groundnut sown together in a 2:8 row ratio in kharif; with cotton it gave about 45 per cent higher net returns than the maize and cowpea block
source: Mahadevaswamy M, Shenoi M M, Ramesh S, Mahadeva C & Venkatesh T, Sustainable livelihood through agro-forestry and livestock based integrated farming system in rainfed Alfisols of Southern Transitional Zone of Karnataka, Agriculture for Sustainable Development 2(2), 2014, pp 97-100

practice_name: Fruit trees with pulse and oilseed intercrops
description: Fruit trees planted 8 x 8 m apart with pulses and castor grown in the spaces to improve soil fertility and give income until the trees start to fruit
source: Mahadevaswamy M, Shenoi M M, Ramesh S, Mahadeva C & Venkatesh T, Sustainable livelihood through agro-forestry and livestock based integrated farming system in rainfed Alfisols of Southern Transitional Zone of Karnataka, Agriculture for Sustainable Development 2(2), 2014, pp 97-100

practice_name: Farm pond for rain water harvesting
description: Excess runoff from the one-acre farm was collected in a small pond of 8 x 8 x 2 m at the lower end of the field to give life-saving or supplemental irrigation
source: Mahadevaswamy M, Shenoi M M, Ramesh S, Mahadeva C & Venkatesh T, Sustainable livelihood through agro-forestry and livestock based integrated farming system in rainfed Alfisols of Southern Transitional Zone of Karnataka, Agriculture for Sustainable Development 2(2), 2014, pp 97-100

practice_name: Groundnut + redgram intercropping in a dry watershed
region: Ramasagara watershed, Molakalmur taluk, Chitradurga, Karnataka
description: Two farmers intercropped groundnut with redgram in kharif 2010-11 in a low and erratic rainfall area where groundnut alone is the usual crop
source: Patil S L, Math S K N, Adhikari R N, Dogra P, Channabasappa K & Reddy K K, Developing an Integrated Farming Systems using Multiple Criteria Decision Making Tools for the Dryland Alfisols in the Deccan Plateau India, Chapter 49 in Natural Resource Conservation: Emerging Issues and Future Challenges (year and pages not confirmed)

practice_name: Pigeonpea + black gram intercropping in organic farms
region: Aland and Gulbarga taluks, Gulbarga district, Karnataka
description: Most organic farmers in the study villages grew pigeonpea with black gram as an intercrop and used farmyard manure and vermicompost and bio-inputs for nutrition and pest control
source: Malgatti M, Resource Utilization Efficiency and Sustainability of Organic Farming in Karnataka, Ph.D. thesis, Indian Agricultural Research Institute New Delhi, 2011

practice_name: Pigeonpea + green gram intercropping in organic farms
region: Aland and Gulbarga taluks, Gulbarga district, Karnataka
description: Organic farmers also grew pigeonpea with green gram as an intercrop; the thesis compared the cost and returns of this system with sole pigeonpea and with conventional farms
source: Malgatti M, Resource Utilization Efficiency and Sustainability of Organic Farming in Karnataka, Ph.D. thesis, Indian Agricultural Research Institute New Delhi, 2011

practice_name: Farm bio-digester botanical pesticide from calotropis neem and datura
region: Tadkal village, Aland taluk, Gulbarga, Karnataka
description: A farmer built a bio-digester to make pesticide from plants that cattle avoid such as calotropis neem and datura and used it against leaf-eating caterpillars and sucking pests
source: Malgatti M, Resource Utilization Efficiency and Sustainability of Organic Farming in Karnataka, Ph.D. thesis, Indian Agricultural Research Institute New Delhi, 2011

practice_name: Neem seed kernel extract spray in organic pigeonpea
region: Tadkal village, Aland taluk, Gulbarga, Karnataka
description: Neem seed kernel extract was sprayed at flowering on an organic pigeonpea crop that also received farmyard manure and compost
source: Malgatti M, Resource Utilization Efficiency and Sustainability of Organic Farming in Karnataka, Ph.D. thesis, Indian Agricultural Research Institute New Delhi, 2011
